general_notes.general_notes:
The paper is a methodological critique of a common practice in normative modeling, not the development or application of a new normative model for clinical prediction.

- association_analysis: "Multifactorial repeated-measures multivariate analyses of variance (ANOVAs) were used to compare regional thickness profiles between groups, with and without global thickness adjustment. Permutation analyses were also conducted."
- key_findings_brief: "Adjusting for global cortical thickness in regional analyses attenuates or eliminates true disease-related cortical thinning in schizophrenia spectrum disorders, leading to erroneous conclusions."
- key_findings_detailed: "The study found that global thickness was reduced in schizophrenia spectrum groups and strongly correlated with regional thickness. When regional thickness was adjusted for global thickness, widespread and significant regional deficits in these groups were either attenuated or completely eliminated. In some cases, this adjustment paradoxically made some regions appear thicker in patient groups. In contrast, adjusting for intracranial volume (ICV) did not have the same detrimental effect. The authors argue that adjusting for global thickness is a flawed approach that obscures true pathology."
- key_limitations: "The sample size for the CHR-P conversion analysis in Study 1 was small. The study is a cautionary tale and a methodological demonstration rather than a clinical application study."
- application_notes: "The authors strongly recommend that future studies examining regional thickness in psychiatric disorders abandon statistical global thickness adjustment and that publicly available analysis tools should provide an option to omit this adjustment."
